definition_en: Clarify service boundaries and domain ownership.
Define fallback, retry, and graceful degradation strategy.
Decision rationale. What architectural decisions were made and why?
Change analysis. What is impacted by a proposed change?
Trade-off reasoning. How are quality attributes balanced?
Economic impact. What are the costs and expected value?
Organizational fit. Are teams aligned with the architecture?
Capability structure. What business capabilities exist and which are critical?
End-to-end workflows. How do business processes execute across domains?
Users and roles. Who interacts with the system and in what roles?
Accountability and governance. Who owns systems, data, and decisions?
Cross-domain influence. How do organizational units influence each other?
Runtime containers. What are the main runtime units?
Internal modularity. How are components structured within containers?
Service responsibility. What capability boundary does each service own?
Technology choices. Which languages, frameworks, and platforms are used?
Interaction mechanisms. How do components communicate?
System boundary. What is inside and outside the system?
Functional decomposition. How are application functions grouped?
Application collaboration. How do applications interact and depend on each other?
Access responsibility. Which roles can access which applications?
Business data movement. How does data support business processes?
Logical schema. How are entities logically related?
Physical schema. How is data physically implemented?
Data transformation. How is data derived and transformed?
Traceability. Where does data originate and propagate?
Ownership and value. What data assets exist and who owns them?
Business entities. What core business entities exist?
Quality assurance. Is data accurate, complete, and timely?
Regulatory paths. Does data usage comply with regulations?
Technical pipelines. How is data processed technically?
Residency constraints. Where is data stored and restricted?
Deployment topology. Where are applications deployed?
Network segmentation. How is the network structured?
Infrastructure layout. What infrastructure components exist?
Scaling and capacity. How are resources allocated and scaled?
Trace controls to policies, systems, and responsible roles.
Document decision rationale and approval trail.
Define backup, restore, and regional failover strategy.
Plan horizontal and vertical scaling with bottleneck controls.
Specify APIs, versioning, and compatibility guarantees.
Capture cross-system dependencies and communication paths.
Business-level integration. How do applications exchange data?
Technical constraints. What latency, throughput, or coupling constraints exist?
Execution semantics. How are requests processed end-to-end?
Action paths. What actions and decisions occur during execution?
Workflow execution. How do workflows orchestrate services?
Call ordering. What is the interaction sequence?
Incident handling. How are incidents managed operationally?
Recovery strategy. What are RPO/RTO objectives?
Reliability targets. What service levels are required?
System visibility. How is system health observed?
Learning loops. How do operations inform evolution?
Map authentication, authorization, and least privilege controls.
Control mechanisms. What controls enforce security policy?
Threat analysis. What threats and risks exist?
Adversarial traversal. How could an attacker move through the system?
Service trust. How do services authenticate each other?
User identity. How are users authenticated?
Access enforcement. Who is authorized to do what?
Regulatory scope. Which regulations apply and where?
